charts.title: SRME by family (0 = experiment)
charts.help: Symmetric relative mean error per stiffness family; 0 means the measured value. The source paper reports the fitted constants themselves (the table below); SRME is this campaign's cross-model metric, not the paper's plot.

charts.title: signed error (model − experiment)
charts.help: The same constants as signed errors, so too-stiff and too-soft read differently — SRME folds both into one magnitude. This is the paper's per-constant on-target figure; its C11 group alone is Figure~\ref{fig:ontarget}.

table.note: |P| is the mean |diagonal| of the residual virial. The lr selection does not read it -- it ranks the tail-mean training loss -- so this column is a check on the reported run, not a gate it passed.

charts.title: SRME by family (0 = experiment)

charts.title: signed error (model − experiment)

eval:ti-elastic:elastic.title: Ti — elastic + pressure — elastic constants across the hcp field
eval:ti-elastic:elastic.sub: scored against the experimental constants AT each temperature; errors averaged per temperature, then over the series

charts.title: mean SRME across the 5 constants
charts.help: This campaign's score, not a plot the paper shows: symmetric relative error against the measured constants at each temperature, averaged over the 5 constants.

charts.title: bulk modulus
charts.help: Voigt–Reuss–Hill polycrystal average of the 5 measured constants — the quantity the paper's Fig. 3a plots. The dashed curve is the paper's digitised measurement.

charts.title: shear modulus
charts.help: Voigt–Reuss–Hill polycrystal average of the 5 measured constants — the quantity the paper's Fig. 3b plots. The dashed curve is the paper's digitised measurement.

charts.title: Poisson ratio
charts.help: Voigt–Reuss–Hill polycrystal average of the 5 measured constants — the quantity the paper's Fig. 3c plots. The dashed curve is the paper's digitised measurement.

charts.title: C11
charts.help: Single-crystal constant against the measured series -- the temperature series of this paper's Figure~\ref{fig:ti-elastic}, which draws these five and no average. The SOURCE paper plots the polycrystal averages (Fig. 3) instead.

charts.title: C33
charts.help: Single-crystal constant against the measured series -- the temperature series of this paper's Figure~\ref{fig:ti-elastic}, which draws these five and no average. The SOURCE paper plots the polycrystal averages (Fig. 3) instead.

charts.title: C44
charts.help: Single-crystal constant against the measured series -- the temperature series of this paper's Figure~\ref{fig:ti-elastic}, which draws these five and no average. The SOURCE paper plots the polycrystal averages (Fig. 3) instead.

charts.title: C12
charts.help: Single-crystal constant against the measured series -- the temperature series of this paper's Figure~\ref{fig:ti-elastic}, which draws these five and no average. The SOURCE paper plots the polycrystal averages (Fig. 3) instead.

charts.title: C13

eval:ti-phase:boxes.title: Ti — equilibrated boxes along the isobars
eval:ti-phase:boxes.sub: the NPT cells the free-energy anchors are built on, not a reported target. `boxes` is complete at 12 files (6 isobar points × 2 phases), so a short row here is a partial measurement and the ΔG beside it rests on fewer points. The anchor columns are the SECOND half of the same gate: finishing a model's boxes moves its cells, which makes every anchor taken in the old ones stale, and DiffTTC stays held until all twelve are re-measured in the current cells

charts.title: hcp — a
charts.help: NPT-averaged lattice parameter along the isobar, with its standard error.

charts.title: hcp — c/a
charts.help: Axial ratio; hcp only, bcc has none.

charts.title: hcp — residual pressure
charts.help: What the barostat actually settled at, minus its target. A free-energy anchor built on a box far from zero here was integrated at the wrong state point.

charts.title: bcc — a
charts.help: NPT-averaged lattice parameter along the isobar, with its standard error.

charts.title: bcc — residual pressure
charts.help: What the barostat actually settled at, minus its target. A free-energy anchor built on a box far from zero here was integrated at the wrong state point.

charts.title: MACE-MPA-0
charts.help: Auxiliary: the source paper reports a phonon DOS (SI Fig. 5c), not this dispersion. The tick marks are Warren's measured neutron modes at the labelled symmetry points.

eval:ti-elastic:phonon.title: ti-elastic — phonon dispersion
eval:ti-elastic:phonon.sub: supercell (5, 5, 3), displacement 0.01 Å; one panel per model, the measurement repeated on each. At the model's own zero-pressure cell, which is what both source protocols use

eval:diamond:stress_strain.title: diamond — stress–strain
eval:diamond:stress_strain.sub: uniaxial deformation; linear-regime slope gives the constants

eval:mgo:stress_strain.title: mgo — stress–strain
eval:mgo:stress_strain.sub: uniaxial deformation; linear-regime slope gives the constants

eval:ti-elastic:bcc.title: Ti — bcc at 1273 K, the phase no fit ever sees
eval:ti-elastic:bcc.sub: ideal 128-atom cell; the band is the spread of three independent measurements

charts.title: stiffness (GPa)
charts.help: The paper's Table 2 comparison: bcc constants at 1273 K against three independent measurements (the band) and the paper's own fused DimeNet++ model (grey bar).

eval:ti-elastic:pressure.title: Ti — hcp lattice constants under hydrostatic pressure
eval:ti-elastic:pressure.sub: 300 K NPT per target pressure, production-averaged cell (paper Fig. 6)

charts.title: c/a
charts.help: Auxiliary: the axial ratio from the two panels above — the compressibility anisotropy in one number. No experimental curve is drawn because the two measured series sample different pressures; read the a and c panels for the measurement.

eval:ti-elastic:liquid.title: Ti — liquid self-diffusion
eval:ti-elastic:liquid.sub: D(T) against the QENS series, pretrained and fine-tuned where a vouched measurement exists; only MACE-MPA-0, MatterSim-v1-5M, Orb-v3, UMA-s-1p2, SevenNet-MF-ompa, PET-MAD-v1.0.2 have any

eval:ti-liquid:sq.title: Ti — liquid structure factor S(q)
eval:ti-liquid:sq.sub: fitted at 1965 K, window-free k-space estimator, scored on q ≥ 2.3 Å⁻¹ (marked); only MACE-MPA-0, MatterSim-v1-5M, Orb-v3, UMA-s-1p2, SevenNet-MF-ompa, PET-MAD-v1.0.2 have any

eval:ti-elastic:dft_test.title: Ti — DFT test set (paper's 5704-configuration data)
eval:ti-elastic:dft_test.sub: errors vs the paper's own DFT labels on the stored subset

eval:ti-phase:free_energy.title: Ti — hcp/bcc free energy along the transition line
eval:ti-phase:free_energy.sub: ΔG(hcp − bcc) at the experimental transition point; positive = bcc already favoured below the transition

charts.title: ΔG(hcp − bcc) along the transition line
charts.help: Frenkel-Ladd anchors at the six statepoints of the experimental hcp-bcc line. Zero is coexistence: the experimental transition temperature is where the paper's target puts ΔG = 0, so distance from the zero line is the error and its SLOPE is a second, independent error.

charts.title: T* from the reversible-scaling crossings
charts.help: Where the two phases' G(T) sweeps cross -- the paper's own route to a transition temperature, with no literature entropy assumed. A pressure is absent when its sweeps were not run or did not cross inside the window they cover; extrapolating two near-parallel free-energy curves would turn a few tenths of a meV into a hundred kelvin.

table.note: ΔG, spread, hysteresis and the pressure imbalance are the AMBIENT point; `anchors` counts how many of the six pressures are measured, and the two T* columns come from the reversible-scaling sweeps, which are the same observable (`fe_rs_*`) and a separate measurement. The experimental slope is fitted through the pressures that crossed, so a model measured on two of six is not compared against a six-point line.

train:diamond:exp_only.title: diamond · exp_only — training
train:diamond:exp_only.sub: Per-epoch history.json. The tail-5 loss column is what selects the rate; the SRME here is the 2 fs reweighted trajectory's own estimate, NOT the reported evaluation — the two disagreed by 17% on MACE/diamond, which is why no column here is a gate. Colour = model, dash = learning rate; seed0 is the promoted run and seed1/seed2 are its replicates at the same rate.

charts.title: cumulative regenerations
charts.help: Trajectory regenerations the run has paid for by this epoch, read off its train.log by umlip.trainlog -- the one parse the paper's \trainRegen macros and its training figure also use. A run whose log was reclaimed draws no line here while keeping its history curves.

charts.title: effective sample fraction
charts.help: Fraction of the reweighted trajectory still carrying weight; a statepoint regenerates when this falls under the config's reweight_ratio, so the curve is the sawtooth, not the threshold it bounces off.

The tail-5 loss column is what selects the rate; the SRME here is the 2 fs reweighted trajectory's own estimate, NOT the reported evaluation — the two disagreed by 17% on MACE/diamond, which is why no column here is a gate. Colour = model, dash = learning rate; seed0 is the promoted run and seed1/seed2 are its replicates at the same rate.

charts.title: cumulative regenerations
charts.help: Trajectory regenerations the run has paid for by this epoch, read off its train.log by umlip.trainlog -- the one parse the paper's \trainRegen macros and its training figure also use. A run whose log was reclaimed draws no line here while keeping its history curves.

charts.title: effective sample fraction
charts.help: Fraction of the reweighted trajectory still carrying weight; a statepoint regenerates when this falls under the config's reweight_ratio, so the curve is the sawtooth, not the threshold it bounces off.
